title: Prime-power Gysin classes on regular schemes and their localizations
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and let $u:U\to V$ be a separated compactifiable finite-type morphism between regular affine Noetherian excellent schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use ordinary etale exceptional pullback [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] and signed roots-of-unity twists [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. Locally $u$ factors as a regular closed immersion followed by a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Here a regular closed immersion has ideal locally generated by a finite sequence each of whose elements is a nonzerodivisor modulo its predecessors. Its codimension is the length of this sequence. The virtual relative dimension $e$ is the smooth relative dimension minus that codimension. If $V=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $U$ is integral, $e=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(\eta_U)$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field]. There is an isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Cl}_u:\Lambda_U(e)[2e]\xrightarrow{\sim}u^!\Lambda_V.$$
For a regular closed immersion it is the absolute-purity fundamental class: locally it is the product of the codimension-one Kummer boundary classes of a defining regular sequence. For a smooth morphism it is the diagonal/deformation orientation of [lem-trf-ambient-diagonal-purity-base-change]. For a factorization it is the composite of these two classes. It is independent of the factorization and of the regular sequence, commutes with etale localization, source and target open restriction, and regular change of base. For composable such regular morphisms $U\xrightarrow uV\xrightarrow vW$, under exceptional transitivity and the canonical twist identifications,
$$\operatorname{Cl}_{vu}=u^!(\operatorname{Cl}_v)\circ\operatorname{Cl}_u(e_v)[2e_v].$$
The same statements hold for essentially finite-type morphisms obtained by localizing these regular schemes, using the model restrictions of [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus]; in particular they apply to finitely generated towers of fields. For a finite purely inseparable extension $L/K$ in characteristic $p\ne\ell$, the class of $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is multiplication by $[L:K]$ under the tautological etale equivalence $a^!\Lambda_K\cong\Lambda_L$. Thus it is a unit, but it is not in general the identity.
